items.title: The Marks of Giving — How a True Bodhisattva Is Recognised Through Generosity

items.zh: 謂諸菩薩本性樂施，於諸現有堪所施物，恒常無間性能於他平等分布，心喜施與，意無追悔。施物雖少，而能均布；惠施廣大，而非狹小。無所惠施，深懷慚恥。常好為他讚施勸施，見能施者心懷喜悅。
items.en: Bodhisattvas are by nature inclined to give; with respect to whatever suitable object is presently at hand to give, they constantly and without interruption distribute it equally to others, the mind delighting in the giving, with no regret afterwards … even when what is given is little, it is still distributed evenly; the intention to give is vast, never narrow or small … when there is nothing to give, one feels deep shame; one constantly delights in praising others' giving and encouraging it, and, seeing another able to give, the heart fills with joy.

items.zh: 於諸尊重、耆宿、福田、應供養者，從座而起，恭敬奉施。於其彼彼此世他世有情無罪利益事中，若請不請，如理為說。若諸有情怖於王賊及水火等，施以無畏，能於種種常極怖中，隨力濟拔。
受他寄物，未嘗差違。若負他債，終不抵誑。於共財所，亦無欺罔。於其種種末尼、真珠、琉璃、螺貝、壁玉、珊瑚、金銀等寶資生具中心迷倒者，能正開悟。尚不令他欺罔於彼，況當自為。其性好樂廣大財位，於彼一切廣大資財心好受用；樂大事業，非狹小門。於諸世間酒色、博戲、歌舞、倡伎種種變現耽著事中，速疾厭捨，深生慚愧。得大財寶，尚不貪著，何況小利。
items.en: Receiving something entrusted by another, one never mishandles it; owing a debt to another, one never denies or deceives; in property jointly held, there is likewise no cheating … by nature one delights in vast wealth and standing, taking genuine pleasure in putting all such vast resources to use; one delights in great undertakings, not narrow or petty ones. Amid the world's intoxicating entanglements — drink, sensual pleasure, gambling, song, dance, entertainment — one swiftly grows weary of them and abandons them, feeling deep shame; even great wealth, once obtained, is never clung to, much less some small gain.

items.zh: 如是等類，當知名為菩薩施波羅蜜多種姓相。云何菩薩戒波羅蜜多種姓相？謂諸菩薩，本性成就軟品不善身語意業，不極暴惡，於諸有情不極損惱。雖作惡業，速疾能悔，常行恥愧，不生歡喜。不以刀杖手塊等事惱害有情；於諸眾生，性常慈愛。於所應敬，時起奉迎，合掌問訊，現前禮拜。修和敬業，所作機捷，非為愚鈍，善順他心。常先含笑，舒顏平視，遠離顰，蹙，先言問訊。

items.title: The Marks of Precepts — A Discipline Measured by Benefit to Others, Not Rule-Following Alone

items.zh: 於恩有情，知恩知報。於來求者常行質直，不以諂誑而推謝之。如法求財，不以非法，不以卒暴。性常喜樂修諸福業。於他修福尚能獎助，況不自為。若見若聞他所受苦，所謂殺縛、割截、捶打、訶毀、迫脅，於是等苦過於自受，重於法受及重後世。於少罪中尚深見怖，何況多罪。
items.en: Towards beings who have shown kindness, one knows that kindness and repays it … one seeks wealth lawfully, never unlawfully, never through violence … by nature one constantly delights in cultivating meritorious deeds … seeing or hearing of another's suffering … one feels that suffering more keenly than one's own, more heavily even than the one who undergoes it, and gives weight to future lives; even the smallest wrongdoing is deeply feared, let alone a greater one.

items.zh: 於他種種所應作事，所謂商、農、放牧、事王、書印、算數、善和諍訟、追求財寶、守護儲積、方便出息，及以捨施、婚姻、集會。於是一切如法事中，悉與同事。於他種種鬪訟諍競，或餘所有互相惱害，能令自他無義無益，受諸苦惱。如是一切非法事中，不與同事。善能制止所不應作。謂十種惡不善業道。不違他命，善順於他同忍同戒。於他事業隨彼所欲，廢己所作而為成辦。
其心溫潤、其心純淨，恚心、害心不久相續，隨生隨捨，起賢善心。尊重實語，不誑惑他，不離他親，亦不好樂，不輕爾說無義無利不相應語。言常柔軟，無有麁獷；於己僮僕尚無苦言，況於他所。敬愛有德，如實讚彼。
items.en: The mind is warm and gentle, pure and clear; anger and the wish to harm never last long or continue, arising only to be released, replaced by a wholesome heart … one values truthful speech, never deceiving others, never dividing those who are close … speech is always soft, never coarse; not even a harsh word for one's own servants, let alone anyone else. One honours and loves the virtuous, praising them exactly as they truly are.

items.zh: 如是等類，當知名為菩薩戒波羅蜜多種姓相。云何菩薩忍波羅蜜多種姓相？

items.title: Patience's Marks, and Diligence's Five Faces — From Rising Before Dawn to Never Being Satisfied

items.zh: 謂諸菩薩，性於他所遭不饒益，無恚害心，亦不反報。若他諫謝，速能納受，終不結恨，不久懷怨。
items.en: Bodhisattvas, by nature, when harmed by another, hold no anger or wish to injure in return, nor do they retaliate. If the other later repents and apologises, one accepts it readily, never harbouring resentment or nursing a grudge for long.

items.zh: 如是等類，當知名為菩薩忍波羅蜜多種姓相。云何菩薩精進波羅蜜多種姓相？
謂諸菩薩，性自翹勤，夙興晚寐，不深耽樂睡眠倚樂。於所作事勇決樂為，不生懈怠，思擇方便，要令究竟。凡所施為一切事業，堅固決定；若未皆作、未皆究竟，終不中間懈廢退屈。於諸廣大第一義中，心無怯弱，不自輕蔑，發勇猛心；我今有力能證於彼。或入大眾，或與他人共相擊論，或餘種種難行事業，皆無畏憚。
items.en: Bodhisattvas, by their very nature, exert themselves — rising early, retiring late, never indulging deeply in the pleasure of sleep or reclining ease … whatever is undertaken is done boldly and gladly, never with laziness, choosing the right means beforehand so the task reaches genuine completion … with respect to the vast, ultimate goal, the mind holds no timidity, never belittling itself … whether entering a large assembly, debating others directly, or facing any other difficult undertaking, there is no fear or hesitation.

blocks.text: How can one recognise someone of the bodhisattva lineage, even before they have made a vow? By natural tendencies towards the six perfections. Two short passages are untranslated.

"By nature inclined to give: whatever suitable thing is at hand, they constantly distribute it equally, the mind delighting in giving, with no regret afterwards." "Even when what is given is little, it is distributed evenly; the intention is vast." "Receiving something entrusted, one never mishandles it; owing a debt, one never denies it." Such a person is not drawn to "drink, sensual pleasure, gambling, song, dance".

"Towards those who have shown kindness, one repays it." "One seeks wealth lawfully, never through violence." Seeing another suffer, "one feels it more keenly than one's own". "Even the smallest wrongdoing is deeply feared." "The mind is warm and gentle; anger and the wish to harm never last long." "One values truthful speech, never dividing those who are close."
"When harmed by another, they hold no anger in return, nor retaliate. If the other later apologises, one accepts it readily, never nursing a grudge."

"Rising early, retiring late, never indulging deeply in sleep"; "whatever is undertaken is done boldly and gladly, choosing the right means first"; "with respect to the vast, ultimate goal, the mind holds no timidity, never belittling itself". Venerable Miào Jìng: timidity is feeling the goal is too great for oneself.
These are not rules but portraits: tendencies that show a person is already oriented towards the bodhisattva path. Many readers will recognise themselves in some of them, and not in others.

quiz.q: "The mind delighting in giving, with no regret." How does Master Cháng Bǎi divide before, during, after?
options: joy before, purity during, no regret after
quiz.why: "They constantly and without interruption distribute it equally to others, the mind delighting in the giving, with no regret afterwards." Master Cháng Bǎi: before giving the heart is joyful, while giving it's pure, after giving there's no regret.

quiz.q: "The intention to give is vast, never narrow." How does Venerable Miào Jìng explain vast and narrow?
options: equality is vast; distinguishing foe and friend is narrow
quiz.why: "Even when what is given is little, it is still distributed evenly; the intention to give is vast, never narrow or small." Venerable Miào Jìng: his mind is vast — equality is vast; thinking in terms of foe and friend is narrow.

quiz.q: "Receiving something entrusted, one never mishandles it." How does Venerable Miào Jìng explain?
options: returning it without the slightest shortfall — trustworthy
quiz.why: "Receiving something entrusted by another, one never mishandles it." Venerable Miào Jìng: when returning it, not the slightest bit is off — this shows trustworthiness.

quiz.q: "The mind is warm and gentle (溫潤)." How does Venerable Miào Jìng explain 潤?
quiz.why: "The mind is warm and gentle, pure and clear; anger and the wish to harm never last long." Venerable Miào Jìng: always being willing to benefit others is called 潤.

quiz.q: "Even the smallest wrongdoing is deeply feared." The note calls "bodhisattvas fear causes, beings fear results" the treatise's own gloss. What does Master Cháng Bǎi say?
options: it's Venerable Miào Jìng's explanation quoted in the lecture; also, the cause must be true, or the fruit goes crooked
quiz.why: "Even the smallest wrongdoing is deeply feared, let alone a greater one." Master Cháng Bǎi: hence, bodhisattvas fear causes, beings fear results. Also: the causal ground must be true; if not, the fruit turns crooked. These are Venerable Miào Jìng's words quoted in the lecture, not the treatise's.

quiz.q: "Never harbouring resentment, nor a grudge for long." How does Venerable Miào Jìng explain?
options: resentment doesn't last — one recovers on one's own
quiz.why: "If the other later repents and apologises, one accepts it readily, never harbouring resentment or nursing a grudge for long." Venerable Miào Jìng: even if resentment arises, it doesn't last long; one recovers by oneself.

quiz.q: "Towards the vast, ultimate goal (廣大第一義), no timidity." How do the masters read it?
options: Miào Jìng: confidence to realise ultimate truth; Cháng Bǎi: the fruit of great awakening
quiz.why: "With respect to the vast, ultimate goal, the mind holds no timidity, never belittling itself." Venerable Miào Jìng: "I'm capable of realising the ultimate truth" — having that confidence is "unflagging diligence." Master Cháng Bǎi: it describes the fruit of unsurpassed great awakening — the so-called vast ultimate.
